This is the third criminal appeal filed by the appellant under Section 14- A(2) of the Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act for grant of regular bail relating to Crime No. 12 of 2023 registered at Police Station Satanbada, District Shivpuri (M.P.) for the offence under Sections 376, 342, 323, 506 of IPC and Sections 3(1)(Da), 3(1)(Dha), 3(2)(V) of the Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act.

Prosecution story in brief is that on 09.01.2023 in evening at 6:00 P.M. prosecutrix was coming from Narwar Lodhi Mata Temple that the appellant with Bolero car came over there and asked Vasudev Sharma vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 18 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/108127958/
1 prosecutrix to drop her to Shivpuri.

entities.text: Vasudev Sharma vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Prosecutrix sat in the car and they went to Satanbada Khurd at the house of the appellant, there the appellant offered her tea and lock the door and commit rape upon her.
The prosecutrix then called Sanjay Kushwah and Janved Parihar and thereafter reported the matter.
Learned counsel for the appellant argued that this is third criminal appeal on behalf of the appellant.

Earlier first criminal appeal was dismissed as withdrawn vide order dated 10.02.2023 passed in Cr.A.No.2298/2023 with liberty to move afresh in the week commencing 12.06.2023 or after recording of statement of prosecutrix before the trial Court whichever is earlier and second criminal appeal was also dismissed as withdrawn vide order dated 08/05/2023 passed in Cr.A.No.5851/2023 with liberty to file afresh after statement of witness Sanjay Kushwah is recorded before the trial Court.
Now, statements of Sanjay Kushwah (PW-3), Janved Parihar (PW-4), have been recorded before the trial Court wherein they have turned hostile and had not supported the case of prosecution.
It is further submitted that the appellant is innocent and has falsely been implicated in this case.
Further argument is that the appellant is in custody since 11.01.2023, the prosecutrix is major.

Investigation is complete and charge-sheet has already been filed, therefore,
there is no requirement of further custodial interrogation of the appellant.
Learned counsel further submits that appellant is permanent resident of District Shivpuri (M.P.) and there is no possibility of his absconsion or tampering with the prosecution evidence.
Hence, learned counsel prays for grant of bail to the appellant.
On the other hand, learned State counsel vehemently opposed the appeal and prayed for its dismissal.
